what: St. Ann's Corner of Harm Reduction provides a South Bronx health hub with overdose prevention, sterile supplies, buprenorphine access and ongoing care coordination.
Meals, hygiene, outreach and a current workforce initiative support many of the same participants, so their health and economic effects need a shared cohort and clear accounting.
We examine additional integrated engagement supported by an ordinary gift, with the whole recipient's costs and net household resources rather than the retail value of free supplies.
strengths: Current clinical, outreach and LUCHA workforce pages identify concrete services and current enrollment, rather than only a historical mission statement.
Three original annual returns reconcile the full recipient's operating and event costs and reveal its reliance on government grants.
One unique-person survival comparison and signed household-resource ledger avoid assigning every rescue another lifetime or treating every free item as a cash saving.
reservations: No current unique clinical cohort, retained-treatment series, net employment outcomes or gift-funded engagement queue was found; outcome and capacity priors remain judgments.
NYC supplies free naloxone and other providers continue care, so extra distribution or a referral does not prove an incremental health benefit.
The conditional estimate is about $22.3 million per better life; net household-resource effects are slightly negative centrally, and low-benefit or adverse scenarios have no positive finite price.

sections.what:
The ordinary charitable recipient is St. Ann's Corner of Harm Reduction Inc., EIN 13-3724008, as its [donation page](https://www.sachr.org/donate) confirms. Its South Bronx hub offers overdose prevention, sterile supplies, HIV/HCV testing and treatment linkage, buprenorphine and wound care. The [current programs](https://www.sachr.org/program) also describe meals, hygiene and behavioral care; these are overlapping services for the same people, not separate additive patient populations. The site includes nonstandard holistic modalities; this model does not assign acupuncture, Reiki or every social activity a clinical effect.

The [LUCHA workforce page](https://www.sachr.org/workforce-development), retrieved directly when the browser wrapper failed, advertises eight weekly sessions, job readiness, financial/computer literacy, interview and resume support, coaching and summer/fall 2026 and winter 2027 enrollment options. It identifies Hispanic Federation and Fund for the City of New York support. That establishes advertised services and a possible employment mechanism, not measured placements or wage gains. This is a whole-recipient gift comparison, not a newly invented restricted clinical/workforce fund.
sections.monitoring:
The [annual-impact page](https://www.sachr.org/annual-impact) still ties 2,816 unique participants, 851,689 services and 24,851 meals to its 2023 report. These are historical reach/output totals. Repeat services, meals, tests and medical contacts are not completed treatments or unique lives saved. The image-only annual-report interpretation from the alpha review is preserved as earlier evidence; it was not freshly visually audited in this revision. Current [drop-in](https://www.sachr.org/drop-in) and workforce pages confirm ongoing offers but do not supply a fresh annual unique cohort.

Useful monitoring would link a privacy-preserving unique cohort to engagement intensity, buprenorphine initiation and retention, alternative-provider access, repeat overdose outcomes, wound/infection outcomes, quality of life, household costs and actual disposable pay. Address-based MSA residency, repeat households, food purchase versus unmet consumption and failed applicants need measurement. A dated additional-staff/slots workplan and covered versus uncovered grant commitments would identify marginal capacity. This review makes no contact or enrollment and treats current scale transfer as a judgment.
sections.qualitative:
The clinical case is strongest for maintaining access to effective opioid treatment and timely overdose response. The [Sordo primary synthesis](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC5421454/fullTextXML) associates treatment with lower mortality, but in/out-treatment contrasts are observational and include treatment selection, cycling and older drug markets. Its buprenorphine rates cannot simply become a local hub effect. A [British Columbia fentanyl-era cohort](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC7190018/fullTextXML) supports retention relevance while remaining an observational comparison in a different health system.

Contemporary implementation evidence constrains optimism. The original HEALing Communities mortality trial, retained from alpha, found no statistically significant mortality reduction; the newly read [2025 secondary randomized analysis](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12302724/) found no improvement in MOUD receipt, 180-day retention or linkage after relevant acute-care encounters. Community-wide implementation differs from SACHR's selected participants, but a promising bundle does not guarantee causal uptake. We therefore use modest explicitly judged mortality/utility differences and retain zero and adverse alternatives.

The central utility change represents residual clinical/function benefit among people alive in both worlds. It is not an independently measured generic utility effect or a claim that every social service improves health. Food, consumption and workforce channels are separately signed; half of positive economic welfare is retained to limit overlap with generic wellbeing, while negative cash burdens remain fully charged. Survival benefits do not receive extra ordinary lifetime earnings. Dignity, HIV/HCV transmission, housing navigation and broader employment/community effects remain unpriced, rather than assumed literally absent. This is a partial conditional research model, not a complete expected-value estimate or donor-ready recommendation.
sections.cost:
Our conditional estimate is about **$22.3 million per better life**: ten combined healthy-year and household-resource equivalents for NYC metro residents. The initial health-only estimate was $13.5 million. The revision changes clinical assumptions, survival accounting, delay and harms as well as adding net household resources; it does not mean measured performance deteriorated.

**What additional money could provide.** The latest full-recipient annual cost is $5.27 million. Applying a judgment about current scale to historical unique reach implies roughly $2,338 in average organizational support per annual engagement equivalent. With an assumed 25% funding response, that becomes about $9,353 in donor funding per additional engagement. These are conditional calculations, not verified marginal prices, additional treatment completions or available slots. Shared administration, fundraising and event expenses enter the denominator once.

**Health benefits.** The central case assumes a modest one-year reduction in mortality among a high-risk subgroup, plus a small improvement in clinical functioning among people alive in both worlds. Treatment starts after three months; the survival comparison is capped at ten years, with no permanent mortality reduction or separate lifetime credit for each overdose rescue. High- and lower-risk groups have different baseline hazards, replacing the initial uniform 8% annual hazard. A small independent health burden remains even when clinical benefits disappear. These are explicit judgments, not locally measured treatment effects.

**Net household resources.** The model distinguishes households whose meals and hygiene supplies replace purchases from households receiving otherwise unmet consumption. It subtracts additional travel costs, actually lost disposable pay and medicine or copay costs after assistance and alternative care. A small workforce-response scenario adds net disposable earnings after taxes, benefits, work expenses and other-provider substitution. SACHR's workforce page establishes an offered program, not a measured placement or wage effect. Free naloxone receives no automatic retail purchase-saving credit.

Following [Coefficient Giving's logarithmic comparison](https://coefficientgiving.org/research/cost-effectiveness/), the economic calculation uses a judged $20,000 annual household-resource baseline and converts dated net resource changes into healthy-year equivalents. Baseline survival, NYC attribution and discounting apply once. Half of positive economic welfare is retained to limit overlap with generic wellbeing; negative resource burdens remain fully charged. Newly surviving participants receive no additional credit for ordinary baseline earnings. Actual purchases, unmet consumption and nested medical payments use a shared cash ledger to avoid duplicate benefits or inconsistent logarithms.

At a $10,000 mathematical normalization—not a gift recommendation—the central model produces about 0.00461 health years and −0.00013 income-equivalent years, or 0.00448 combined years. Scaling costs and engagement together leaves the price unchanged. Every assumption and signed pathway is recorded in the appendix.

**Uncertainty and scope.** A favorable bundled scenario is approximately $1.57 million per better life; a weak-response, higher-burden scenario is net negative. Zero expansion gives zero effects. Clinical-null and complete clinical-substitution cases retain costs and harms. A selected external-resource companion adds $2,000 per additional engagement for unrecognized clinical, public-stock and volunteer inputs, giving approximately $27.1 million at the same welfare result; this is not a complete net societal-cost estimate. No duplicate procurement expense or public-stock saving is added. Unmeasured other-program effects and actual funding response could dominate this partial model.
sections.funding:
The three original returns were freshly retrieved directly; the browser wrapper failed. Fiscal periods are July 2022–June 2023, July 2023–June 2024 and July 2024–June 2025. Full-recipient gross expense is **$4,348,379/$5,106,419/$5,267,469**, adding direct fundraising-event costs $73,846/$115,347/$95,881 to Part IX totals $4,274,533/$4,991,072/$5,171,588. The comparable annual mean is $4,907,422.33. The 2025 functional amounts $4,384,865 program, $602,749 management and $183,974 fundraising reconcile to Part IX, with direct events added once. [2023 original](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202421369349307717/IRS990) [2024 original](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202531299349302658/IRS990) [2025 original](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202630649349300233/IRS990)

Recognized noncash gifts $94,661/$95,182/$109,444 are not added again to reported expense merely because they are noncash. Latest [Schedule D](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/full_text/202630649349300233/IRS990 ScheduleD) reconciles audit expense to Part IX without extra donated-service adjustment. Actual audit opinion/control findings were not newly reviewed; a Form 990 statement that an audit exists is not a fresh independent-audit acceptance. Latest government grants $4,469,690 dominate support; revenue $4,828,637 is net of event expense while the chosen gross cost denominator adds that expense back. The $342,951 deficit is unchanged when gross revenue/cost are treated consistently.

The 2025 balance sheet reports $291,414 cash, $1,940,700 pledges/grants receivable and $2,113,536 net assets without donor restrictions. Receivables, lease right-of-use assets/liabilities and equipment mean unrestricted net assets are not cash runway or proof of spare operating capacity. Grant timing, renewals, current restricted commitments, actual staffing/clinical slots and replacement funding are missing. A deficit suggests continuity questions, not a verified next-dollar treatment opportunity.

NYC's [current provider route](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/health/health-topics/naloxone.page) provides free naloxone and fentanyl strips to registered OOPPs. Its [May 2026 mail campaign](https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/about/press/pr 2026/free-naloxone-by-mail-campaign.page) reports285,000 kits distributed citywide in 2025 and free mail/community routes. Supplies alone cannot identify SACHR's unique engagement or donor return. The workforce page names existing funders without grant amounts; no additional support package or available capacity is verified. No donation, contact, form submission or new restricted-gift arrangement was made.

historicalAlphaModel.formula: k=ln(1+d); F(v,t)=(1-exp(-v*t))/v; B=u*[F(m-delta+k,1)-F(m+k,1)+(exp(-(m-delta))-exp(-m))*exp(-k)*F(m+k,T-1)]; M=p*v*[z*F(m-delta+k,1)+(1-z)*F(m+k,1)]; Qall=N*f*a*b*(z*B+M)-h; QMSA=g*Qall; price10=10*C/QMSA when positive.
historicalAlphaModel.counterfactual: Existing public grants, other harm-reduction services and medical care continue. a discounts replacement by alternative services; b separately discounts whether unrestricted funding changes the supported scale. Neither is reapplied per mechanism.
historicalAlphaModel.attribution: One unique cohort and a combined mortality effect prevent repeat-rescue and overlapping-service lifetime double counting. Mortality and short-lived utility changes are distinct terms on the same survival curve.
historicalAlphaModel.uncertainty: Reasoned integrated clinical scenario, not a measured program effect or comprehensive social return. No source-calibrated probability is claimed; broad alternatives, complete substitution and adverse outcomes are explicit.
historicalAlphaModel.nativeOutcomes: Unique participants -> additional integrated harm-reduction/clinical engagement -> one-year mortality-hazard and utility changes -> finite survival-adjusted QALYs. Central annual normalization transfers 2,816 older participants to 2,252.8 current-equivalent participants; after care and funding additionality, 281.6 integrated-engagement equivalents remain, including 168.96 higher-risk equivalents. Whole-recipient cost per additional engagement is $18705.50 and per local equivalent $19087.25. These are judgment-based native units, not observed retained buprenorphine patients or additional rescues. Mortality and morbidity components contribute 1.9876 and 2.0022 all-population QALYs.
